question: Are NYC's streets more dangerous at night? Make a chart and give a conclusion for a news report.

options.metric: percentage of eligible crashes with at least one person injured or killed (number_of_persons_injured > 0 or number_of_persons_killed > 0)
options.denominator: eligible police-reported crashes in each time group; both person-outcome counts must be nonmissing
options.grouping: Night = 20:00:00-23:59:59 and 00:00:01-05:59:59; daytime = 06:00:00-19:59:59; exact 00:00:00 is shown separately as a potential default-time group
options.reason: A per-crash share directly compares how often a reported crash involved casualties across clock-time periods.
options.answer: Among eligible NYC police-reported crashes in 2013–2025, 28.6% of night crashes involved injury or death versus 23.4% of daytime crashes, while exact-midnight records were 26.7% in a separate group.
options.interpretation: Night means 20:00:00–23:59:59 plus 00:00:01–05:59:59, daytime means 06:00:00–19:59:59, and exact 00:00:00 is separate; among 2013–2025 eligible crashes, 28.6% of night crashes (143,039/500,924) involved at least one injured or killed person versus 23.4% of daytime crashes (376,361/1,607,466), with 26.7% in the separate midnight group (6,360/23,786). Comparing injury-or-death involvement per reported crash is a defensible way to compare casualty likelihood conditional on a crash, and the observed share is higher at night. This does not establish danger per trip or road user because the data contain no traffic or travel exposure, and the validity of exact-midnight timestamps is uncertain. Checks found 0 missing dates and 0 missing times in the complete years; 42 of 2,132,218 dated crashes were excluded for missing injured/killed counts (18 and 36 missing entries, with overlap), 136,969 rows from partial 2012 and 2026 were excluded, and exact-midnight records were retained separately (23,787 candidates, 23,786 passing the outcome filters).

options.metric: mean number of persons injured plus persons killed per eligible crash
options.denominator: eligible police-reported crashes in each time group; both person-outcome counts must be nonmissing
options.grouping: Night = 20:00:00-23:59:59 and 00:00:01-05:59:59; daytime = 06:00:00-19:59:59; exact 00:00:00 is shown separately as a potential default-time group
options.reason: Mean injured and killed persons per crash captures the recorded casualty burden, including multiple casualties in a single crash.
options.answer: Eligible night crashes averaged 0.409 people injured or killed per crash in 2013–2025, compared with 0.310 for daytime crashes; the separate exact-midnight group averaged 0.359.
options.interpretation: Night means 20:00:00–23:59:59 plus 00:00:01–05:59:59, daytime means 06:00:00–19:59:59, and exact 00:00:00 is separate; among eligible 2013–2025 crashes, the mean of persons injured plus persons killed was 0.409 per night crash, 0.310 per daytime crash, and 0.359 per exact-midnight crash. This measure is defensible because it captures the average recorded casualty burden per crash, including crashes with multiple casualties, and it is higher at night. It cannot establish danger per trip or road user because the data contain no traffic or travel exposure, and exact-midnight timestamps may be defaults. Checks found 0 missing dates and 0 missing times in the complete years; 42 of 2,132,218 dated crashes were excluded for missing injured/killed counts (18 and 36 missing entries, with overlap), 136,969 rows from partial 2012 and 2026 were excluded, and exact-midnight records were retained separately (23,787 candidates, 23,786 passing the outcome filters).

answer: 1.
